newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy not seen making EMU start - Germany's Henkel.
newsitem.headline: Italy not seen making EMU start - Germany's Henkel.

text.p: Italy has made big efforts to consolidate its debt but Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government lacks the support to make real reforms of the welfare state needed to ensure its early entry into the single European currency, Germany's Hans-Olaf Henkel said.
Henkel, head of the Federation of German Industry (BDI), made the comments in an interview to appear in Italian business weekly magazine Il Mondo to be published on Saturday.
"The efforts of the Prodi government to consolidate debt have been impressive. But I believe Prodi does not have the necessary support to get a major reform of the welfare state under way.
"And without that I am convinced that it will be difficult for Italy to join monetary union, at least at the start," Henkel was quoted as saying.

Henkel said Maastricht criteria should be interpreted on a trend basis "and that even countries which slightly deviated from the three percent parameter but which had ready a credible and solid plan to reduce deficit and debt should be accepted."
"I think it would perhaps be possible to get the agreement of all European partners on this kind of interpretation," he added.

"The hypothesis of a delay in the single currency is very probable," he said. "But putting off the date would have ominous consequences for all countries because the European Union has not planned any safety net for such an eventuality.
"Not even Germany would emerge unharmed," he added.
Among the reasons making a delay probable, Henkel said, was the victory of the left in French elections which had sown doubt among Germans over the rigour of the new Jospin government.
